blocks.text: Ibumba is the Kinyarwanda word for clay. Ours is dug near Gatagara, where potters have worked the same banks for generations, and every piece we sell began there.

steps.title: Wedge
steps.text: The clay is kneaded until it is even all the way through, so it holds together on the wheel and in the fire.

steps.title: Throw
steps.text: On the wheel the lump is centred, opened and pulled up into a wall, a little thinner with every pass.

steps.title: Trim and dry
steps.text: Once it is leather-hard the foot is cut, and the piece dries slowly for a week under cloth.

steps.title: Fire
steps.text: Two firings: one to harden it, and one to melt the glaze into glass. The kiln decides the rest.

blocks.quote: I came for one evening and stayed for the whole season. My kitchen is full of slightly wonky bowls and I love every one of them.
blocks.name: Aline Uwase

blocks.text: Restaurants and cafes in Kigali serve on our plates. If you need a set made for your table, write to us and we will throw a sample.
